name: The Citadel of Markor
desc:
The Citadel of Markor, also known as the Markor Citadel, is possibly the most prominent research organization in Lumen, the Citadel pride themselves as the foremost keepers of knowledge, history, and research into Lumen and the surrounding [Depths](location:the_depths). The Citadel was founded 500 years into the Resurgence and receives the majority of its funding from [the Central Authority](faction:the_central_authority), a contribution that [the Authority](faction:the_central_authority) claims falls in line with their desire for global unity, and for a united front against [the Depths](location:the_depths).

Their researches include: History documentation, [Depths](location:the_depths)\-delving, restoration of ancient texts, documentation of attunement usage in the everyday life of the Lumensfolk, and documentation of different cultures across Lumen.

As well as an archive, the Citadel is also an institute of education where people can take courses to improve their skills, such as cosmetic surgery.

Due to the cultural and historical importance of the Citadel, the global calendar calculates the date based on the time relative to the founding of the Citadel. Years after its founding use "CE" (Citadel Era), while those before it are designated "BCE".

57 years after its initial founding, the Citadel established [The Citadel Divers](faction:the_divers) in response to reports of individuals returning from the Depths, theorizing that they could deploy agents to the Depths directly to coordinate research, recon, and offensive action.

In 108 CE, a fire broke out in the Citadel's archives, destroying some of their records, many of which concerned the early history of the Citadel.
additional_info:
-   The Citadel of Markor is loosely based off of the Mouseion of Alexandria, a large, ancient institution that was notable for its research into various arts and sciences.
    -   The Library of Alexandria was part of the institution as well.
        -   An incident in 48 BCE involved Julius Caesar's soldiers setting fire to ships, which later spread and destroyed a portion of the library. This may also reflect on the fire that occurred in the Markor Citadel.
